title: Corpus slices
description: triage-slices' (code) output: the catalogue's admissible candidates, packed into byte-bounded slices ahead of the dispositions fan-out. One shard on disk per slice (00-slices/<id>.json) mirrors this array's candidate_ids; refs.check_slices holds the two to the same partition of the catalogue.

cap_bytes.description: The byte budget every slice was packed against. Echoed here (rather than only in the catalogue's policy) so a reader auditing one slice's bytes against the cap does not have to open a second file.

phase.description: The run's phase declaration, as `triage-slices --phase N --defer-kind KIND` declared it. This is the FIRST of the four artifacts that carry it, and the only one that carries it by declaration rather than by copy -- triage-seal, intake and reconcile-seal each read it from their predecessor. Absent when no phase was declared, which is what makes a plan for an unphased run byte-identical to one written before this field existed. deferred_count is absent here for the reason $defs/phase gives: the deferred set is enumerated per slice below, and a count beside it would be a second spelling of a length.

catalogue_facts.description: Everything rb-triage-objective may know about 00-catalogue.json without opening it, so that pass's reads does not name the catalogue and its dispatch is bounded by max_candidates rather than by corpus size. request and policy are verbatim copies; the other two are derived, and refs.check_slices recomputes both from the catalogue through the same functions that wrote them.

request.description: The catalogue's request, copied verbatim -- so it is held to the catalogue's own definition of it, the way its sibling entries[] already is, rather than to a bare object that would accept a pair catalogue-0.1.json itself would reject. Layer 1 is the only place this contract can live: refs.check_slices recomputes this block's derived numbers and deliberately abstains from its verbatim copies, on the rule that a derived number is arithmetic a reader recomputes while a copy is not testimony.

policy.description: The catalogue's policy, copied verbatim, held to the catalogue's own definition for the reason request is.

excluded.description: The catalogue's excluded array as a tally plus the paths for the four exclusion reasons that embed a disputable judgment. Bounded in bytes, not entries: a count cap without a character bound is the defect open against digest's names.

total.description: Length of the catalogue's excluded array, including entries no path is kept for -- the only thing at gate 0 separating a corpus with 123 binaries from one with none.

by_reason.description: One key per exclusion_reason that occurs, sorted. Reasons that did not occur are absent rather than zero.

entries_truncated.description: Whether the byte budget stopped the entries list short. An unconditional sibling of entries, present as false when it did not bite, following keys_truncated and skeleton_nodes_truncated: a truncation a prompt can see is a fact about the input, and one it cannot see is a lie about it.

candidate_bytes.description: candidate_id -> that candidate's own source bytes, for every catalogue candidate including inadmissible ones. Source size, never a serialized row's size, which saturates once the digest skeleton hits its 128-node clamp.

slices.description: A catalogue with admissible candidates always yields at least one slice; zero here is a slicer defect, not a judgment call.

id.description: Code-minted (s01, s02, ...), short and stable, because it is a path segment: 00-slices/<id>.json and 00-dispositions/<id>.json both join it through safe_segment. The human-readable name belongs in label, not here -- concatenating group names into the id itself produced unreadable strings.

label.description: Human-readable name for this slice, carrying the prose the id deliberately does not.

groups.description: The catalogue groups (signature clusters, directory subtrees, ...) this slice draws candidates from, named in the same vocabulary as provenance[].group.

bytes.description: Total digest bytes of the candidates this slice's SHARD carries -- which is the slice's own candidates minus any in deferred_candidate_ids, since a deferred candidate is subtracted from the shard rather than from the partition. refs.check_slices recomputes this from the shard and checks it matches, so a slice cannot silently drift from its own header, and it is the dispatch's actual read cost, which is what cap_bytes is a cap on. Zero for a fully deferred slice, which has no shard at all.

candidate_ids.description: Every candidate this slice owns. A slice with no candidates would have nothing for a dispositions-part member to rule on, so this floor mirrors the outer slices array's.

deferred_candidate_ids.description: The subset of this slice's candidate_ids that the run's declared phase defers, omitted entirely when it is empty. These stay in candidate_ids -- the partition is total and phase-independent, so slice boundaries mean the same thing in phase 1 and phase 3 -- but are absent from the shard, so no rb-triage-rule member ever sees one and no prompt is asked to apply the policy. A slice whose whole candidate_ids set appears here is fully deferred: no shard is written for it and no disposition part is expected, which is where three of eleven dispatches went on the corpus this was measured against. triage-seal synthesises the defer disposition for every id named here, so the candidate is still ruled on the record.

provenance.description: One entry per group this slice draws from, recording how that group's candidates split across every slice -- so a human at gate 0 can tell a slice boundary that fell mid-cluster from one that did not.

in_this_slice.description: How many of this group's candidates landed in this slice.

in_group_total.description: How many of this group's candidates exist across every slice, so in_this_slice can be read as a fraction without opening the siblings.

other_slices.description: The other slice ids holding the rest of this group's candidates. Empty when in_this_slice equals in_group_total -- the group did not get split.
